title: Phishing Email with Malicious Attachment
description: At 14:30Z, a user in Finance reported a suspicious email masquerading as a vendor invoice. The user downloaded and opened the attached 'invoice_7482.docm' file, which executed a PowerShell script upon enabling macros. The script attempted to harvest credentials and beaconed out to a suspicious IP (198.51.100.45).
root_cause: Employee clicked malicious attachment and enabled macros
resolution: Endpoint isolated, credentials reset, malicious artifacts removed, domain blocklisted.
outcome: Threat contained successfully

title: Secondary Phishing Campaign Targeting Finance
description: Another Finance endpoint exhibited suspicious behavior shortly after the initial incident. A PowerShell process (powershell.exe -ep bypass -w hidden) was spawned by Microsoft Word, indicating another successful phishing payload execution. The process established a connection to the same external IP block (198.51.100.48).
root_cause: Second employee fell for the same phishing campaign
resolution: Endpoint isolated, user credentials rotated, organization-wide email search and purge conducted.
outcome: Threat contained successfully

title: Ransomware Behavior Following Phishing Escalation
description: An escalated variant of the previous phishing payload was executed on a third Finance machine. After initial execution, the malware began modifying file extensions to '.crypt' and attempting to delete volume shadow copies via vssadmin.exe. Connections to a command and control server at 198.51.100.50 were observed.
root_cause: Escalated phishing payload with ransomware capabilities
resolution: Endpoint disconnected from network, affected files restored from offline backups, machine reimaged.
outcome: Threat mitigated with minimal data loss

title: Spearphishing Targeting Executive Level
description: The CEO's executive assistant received a highly targeted email appearing to be from legal counsel. The email contained a link to a credential harvesting site hosted at 203.0.113.88. The user submitted their Office 365 credentials, leading to anomalous login activity from a foreign IP address.
root_cause: Successful spearphishing credential harvest
resolution: Account locked, passwords reset, MFA tokens revoked, and unauthorized inbox rules removed.
outcome: Account secured and unauthorized access terminated

title: PowerShell Dropper Execution
description: An IT workstation alerted on the execution of an obfuscated PowerShell script running directly from memory. The payload attempted to download secondary modules from a pastebin-like site via 192.0.2.115. Antivirus blocked the secondary payload download, but the initial script execution was successful.
root_cause: User executed unverified IT script from untrusted source
resolution: Process terminated, script source blocked at perimeter, endpoint scanned for persistence mechanisms.
outcome: Execution halted before secondary payload delivery

title: Credential Theft via Keylogger
description: A routine EDR scan detected an unknown binary 'sysupdate.exe' hooking into keyboard APIs on a Finance workstation. The process was attempting to log keystrokes and store them in a hidden temporary file. The file contained recent passwords typed by the user, and network logs showed attempts to exfiltrate to 198.51.100.99.
root_cause: Drive-by download installed keylogging malware
resolution: Malware quarantined, all user credentials rotated, workstation quarantined for full forensic analysis.
outcome: Malware removed and compromised credentials invalidated

title: Suspicious VPN Login from Foreign IP
description: A successful VPN authentication was logged for a remote worker from an IP address in a country where the company has no operations (203.0.113.200). The login occurred at 3 AM local time for the user. A 'impossible travel' alert fired, as the user had logged in from their home country just two hours prior.
root_cause: Compromised VPN credentials lacking strict geo-blocking
resolution: VPN session terminated, user account disabled temporarily, geo-blocking rules updated.
outcome: Unauthorized access blocked, user re-authenticated securely

title: Privilege Escalation via Service Account
description: An IT infrastructure server recorded a rapid succession of failed login attempts followed by a successful interactive login using the 'svc_backup' account. The account then executed 'whoami /priv' and attempted to dump LSASS memory. The activity originated from an internal engineering workstation.
root_cause: Service account password reused and compromised
resolution: Service account password rotated, interactive logon disabled for service accounts, source workstation isolated.
outcome: Lateral movement stopped, privileged account secured

title: Lateral Movement Detected via SMB
description: An Engineering workstation was observed initiating numerous SMB connections to other endpoints in the subnet over port 445. The connections attempted to use passed hashes (Pass-the-Hash) to authenticate. Several administrative shares were successfully accessed before network segmentation policies blocked further movement.
root_cause: Compromised engineering workstation used as pivot
resolution: Workstation isolated from network, accessed endpoints scanned for artifacts, lateral movement rules tightened.
outcome: Threat contained to initial subnet

title: Ransomware-like File Encryption
description: An HR representative reported that several local documents were inaccessible and appended with a '.lock' extension. The EDR triggered on rapid file modification events and an unknown process 'update_helper.exe' consuming high CPU. Network traffic indicated key negotiation with 192.0.2.22.
root_cause: User downloaded malicious software disguised as PDF reader update
resolution: Process terminated by EDR, endpoint isolated, encrypted files restored from cloud backup.
outcome: Data recovered, malware eradicated

title: Unusual Outbound Data Transfer
description: The Data Loss Prevention (DLP) system flagged a massive outbound data transfer of 50GB from an R&D workstation to an unknown external IP address (203.0.113.150) over an encrypted tunnel. The transfer occurred outside of normal business hours and involved sensitive proprietary design files.
root_cause: Compromised R&D account attempting data exfiltration
resolution: Network connection terminated, user account suspended, forensic investigation initiated on transferred files.
outcome: Exfiltration partially blocked, investigation ongoing

title: Brute Force Login Attempts
description: The Active Directory domain controllers logged thousands of failed authentication attempts against multiple user accounts over a 10-minute period. The source of the attacks was identified as a compromised IoT device on the guest network attempting to guess weak passwords.
root_cause: Vulnerable IoT device on guest network
resolution: IoT device disconnected, guest network segmentation verified, no accounts compromised.
outcome: Brute force attack thwarted

title: DNS Tunneling Detected
description: The intrusion detection system flagged anomalous DNS traffic originating from an Engineering endpoint. The endpoint was making hundreds of TXT record queries to a specific suspicious domain 'update-chk-sys.com'. The payload sizes and frequency were indicative of a DNS tunneling command and control channel.
root_cause: Malware attempting stealthy C2 via DNS
resolution: Malicious domain sinkholed at DNS server, endpoint isolated and cleaned.
outcome: C2 channel severed, endpoint remediated

title: Malicious Browser Extension
description: A marketing employee reported performance issues and unusual pop-ups in their web browser. An investigation revealed a sideloaded browser extension named 'SEO Optimizer Pro' that was injecting ads and tracking browsing history. The extension was communicating with 198.51.100.10.
root_cause: User bypassed security controls to install unapproved extension
resolution: Extension uninstalled, browser policies enforced to block sideloading, user educated on approved software.
outcome: Malicious extension removed and policy enforced

title: USB Device Policy Violation
description: An endpoint management agent alerted that an unauthorized USB mass storage device was plugged into a Manufacturing floor workstation. The device was automatically blocked by DLP policies, but the user attempted multiple times to bypass the restriction.
root_cause: Employee attempting to use personal USB drive
resolution: Device blocked, user manager notified for policy violation review.
outcome: Policy enforced, no data transferred

title: Unauthorized Cloud Storage Upload
description: Network monitoring detected a large upload of confidential legal documents (approx. 5GB) to a personal, non-corporate cloud storage provider (Mega.nz). The upload was initiated by a Legal department user account, violating data handling policies.
root_cause: User attempting to bypass corporate file sharing tools for convenience
resolution: Upload terminated by web gateway, user reprimanded, access to non-corporate cloud storage blocked.
outcome: Data exfiltration prevented, policies reinforced

title: Supply Chain Compromise Attempt
description: A software update from a trusted vendor in the Procurement department was flagged by the EDR as containing a malicious payload. The installer (vendor_setup_v2.exe) attempted to drop a known backdoor Trojan upon execution. The digital signature of the installer was valid but belonged to a compromised certificate.
root_cause: Compromised vendor software update
resolution: Installation blocked by EDR, vendor notified of compromise, network-wide ban on the specific software version.
outcome: Supply chain attack intercepted before impact

title: Insider Threat - Excessive Data Access
description: A user in the Finance department, who had recently tendered their resignation, was observed accessing and downloading an unusually large number of sensitive financial reports and customer lists. The activity was far outside their normal baseline behavior.
root_cause: Malicious insider attempting data theft prior to departure
resolution: User access immediately revoked, downloaded files securely deleted from local machine, HR involved.
outcome: Data theft prevented, insider threat mitigated

title: Watering Hole Attack via Partner Site
description: Several Business Development employees visited a compromised industry partner website. The site hosted a malicious iframe that attempted to exploit a recent browser vulnerability. EDR telemetry showed the browser process attempting to spawn a suspicious shell process.
root_cause: Compromised third-party website serving exploit kit
resolution: Exploit blocked by EDR, partner notified, website temporarily blocked at corporate firewall.
outcome: Exploitation failed, threat contained

title: API Key Exposure in Public Repo
description: An automated secrets scanning tool detected a corporate AWS API key committed to a public GitHub repository by an Engineering team member. The key had full administrative privileges. Logs showed no unauthorized usage of the key prior to discovery.
root_cause: Accidental commit of sensitive credentials to public repository
resolution: API key revoked immediately, new key generated, repository history rewritten to remove secret.
outcome: Credentials rotated before exploitation

title: Failed Containment - Reboot Without Network Isolation
description: A user on FIN-WS-095 reported suspicious popups after downloading an email attachment. An analyst rebooted the machine without disconnecting from the network. Upon reboot, the malware payload resumed C2 beaconing to 198.51.100.60 and successfully exfiltrated cached browser credentials.
root_cause: Analyst rebooted endpoint without network disconnect, allowing persistence mechanism to execute
resolution: Rebooting without network isolation failed. Required physical network disconnect, forensic triage, and complete re-image.
outcome: Remediation failed initially; containment achieved only after physical network disconnect

title: False Positive - IT Mass Deployment Script Flagged as Ransomware
description: EDR fired critical ransomware alerts on multiple endpoints across IT and Engineering (IT-WS-101, ENG-WS-045). An automated batch script was renaming and updating configuration files across 200 workstations. Investigation confirmed the activity was an approved emergency patch deployment executed by IT Systems Administrator.
root_cause: Legitimate administrative bulk file update matched heuristic ransomware signature
resolution: Activity verified against approved change request CR-8921. Alert closed as false positive, EDR exclusion path added for deployment tool.
outcome: False positive resolved without operational disruption

title: False Positive - Internal Vulnerability Assessment Triggered Brute Force Alert
description: SIEM generated high-severity brute-force alerts from IP 10.10.2.50 against the primary domain controller. Rapid authentication attempts were logged against 50 service accounts. Investigation confirmed the source was an authorized Qualys vulnerability scan scheduled by the InfoSec compliance team.
root_cause: Scheduled authorized security scan matched password spraying detection rule
resolution: Correlated with Security Operations calendar. Added scanner IP to SIEM alert suppression list during maintenance windows.
outcome: Verified benign assessment activity; rules updated to prevent false alarms

title: Ineffective Remediation - Credential Reset Without Session Invalidation
description: Following a credential harvesting alert on EXEC-WS-005, the user password was reset in Active Directory. However, active Azure AD / Entra ID session tokens and OAuth refresh tokens were not revoked. The adversary continued accessing the executive mailbox from an external proxy at 203.0.113.110 for an additional 18 hours.
root_cause: Partial remediation: password was changed but existing session tokens remained valid
resolution: Revoked all active refresh tokens via Revoke-AzureADUserAllRefreshToken cmdlet, forced re-authentication with hardware MFA token.
outcome: Initial password-only reset failed; complete session revocation terminated unauthorized access

title: Supply Chain Phishing Variant Targeting Procurement
description: Procurement specialist on PRO-WS-003 received an email appearing to come from an existing hardware supplier requesting urgent bank detail confirmation. The email contained a malicious macro document that attempted connection to 198.51.100.75 (part of the recurring Finance attack infrastructure).
root_cause: Spearphishing leveraging known vendor identity and shared adversary C2 infrastructure
resolution: Endpoint isolated, 198.51.100.0/24 subnet block verified, vendor security team contacted to notify of domain spoofing.
outcome: Threat neutralized quickly by applying Finance campaign playbook

title: DevOps Hardcoded Secret in Staging Container
description: A container image pushed to the internal registry was found to contain hardcoded database credentials in the Dockerfile layer history. The container had been deployed to the staging Kubernetes cluster accessible from developer VPN.
root_cause: Developer embedded database password in container image build args instead of using Kubernetes secrets
resolution: Staging container terminated, database credentials rotated, CI/CD pipeline updated to enforce pre-commit secret scanning.
outcome: Secret invalidated and CI/CD gate added

title: Mutated Macro Campaign Targeting Legal Department
description: A paralegal on LEG-WS-012 opened an email attachment titled contract_amendment_v3.docm. An obfuscated PowerShell command executed in hidden mode, attempting to beacon out to 198.51.100.92. EDR memory scanning detected process hollowing into svchost.exe.
root_cause: Macro-enabled phishing document executed process hollowing
resolution: Process terminated, endpoint isolated from network, full disk image acquired for forensic analysis.
outcome: Execution halted and malicious artifacts preserved for legal hold

title: Ineffective Remediation - Antivirus Cleaned Dropper but Left Rogue Root CA
description: Following a trojan alert on MKT-WS-030, standard antivirus reported the malicious executable was successfully deleted. However, three days later, users reported SSL certificate warnings. Forensic analysis revealed the original dropper had installed a rogue root Certificate Authority into the Windows certificate store.
root_cause: Antivirus removed binary file but did not audit the local trusted root certificate authority store
resolution: Rogue root CA certificate removed from certmgr.msc, endpoint re-imaged from baseline golden image.
outcome: Standard AV cleanup was ineffective; re-imaging required to ensure certificate integrity

title: False Positive - Developer Automated Backup Flagged as Exfiltration
description: DLP triggered a high-severity alert for 25GB of compressed data uploaded to an external S3 bucket from ENG-WS-188 at 02:00 UTC. Investigation showed a Senior Developer had configured an automated personal backup of local development Docker volumes before hardware replacement.
root_cause: Developer backup script matched external cloud exfiltration heuristic
resolution: Data inspected and confirmed non-proprietary local dev environments. User guided to use corporate OneDrive for approved data migration.
outcome: Verified benign; corporate data transfer guidelines communicated

title: Cloud IAM Privilege Escalation Attempt in Staging
description: CloudTrail logged an anomalous CreatePolicyVersion API call from an IAM user account belonging to an intern. The policy grant attempted to attach AdministratorAccess to the intern role. The request originated from an unfamiliar IP address 192.0.2.180.
root_cause: Compromised intern IAM access key used for privilege escalation attempt
resolution: IAM user deactivated, API keys revoked, SCP (Service Control Policy) applied to prevent privilege escalation on intern roles.
outcome: Escalation blocked by IAM boundary policy; compromised credentials invalidated
